newsitem.title: GERMANY: African coffee growers should raise yields-Rothfos.
newsitem.headline: African coffee growers should raise yields-Rothfos.

text.p: African coffee growers should exploit low production costs to raise yields and place their products in the world market, Jens Janecki, a senior manager at German coffee trader Bernhardt Rothfos GmbH, said on Wednesday.

Since Asia had a similar potential, African producers should focus more on arabicas, where Asia had climatic disadvantages and where it was easier to compete, he told the Licht World Coffee Conference.
"...Africa has optimistic perspectives for the future, Uganda is leading the way. Positive first steps are also seen in Ethiopia, Kenya and Tanzania," Janecki said.

Rothfos data going back to the 1980/81 crop year showed African countries in their strongest years had produced an average 9.77 million bags of arabicas and 16.46 million of robustas, a total of 26.22 million.
By contrast, Rothfos forecast actual African output in 1996/97 at 7.82 million bags of arabicas and 10.56 million bags of robustas.
Production costs in Latin America of above $1,500 per tonne compared with $750 in Uganda, $447 in Cameroon and $355 in Indonesia, it said.
But Africa's coffee industries needed to be privatised and monetary policies liberalised. Farming methods needed improving and milling and export infrastructures left much to be desired.
